newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares suffer heavy losses for 3rd day.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares suffer heavy losses for 3rd day.

text.p: The Slovenian SBI index extended hefty losses on Thursday, falling 6.19 percent to take its losses to 21.8 percent in three days.
The SBI ended 85.4 points lower at 1,295.26 after hitting an all-time high of 1,655.35 on Monday.
But traders said they expect the market to steady on Friday, as it had already recovered well from an early morning lows of 1,270.35 points.
The market fell plumbed such lows as market participants continued to cash in profits amid general confusion over the central bank's ruling to restrict foreign trading activity.

The Bank of Slovenia on Tuesday said foreign portfolio investors would have to open a special custody or fiduciary account at one of Slovenia's 14 fully licensed banks in order to trade in domestic securities.
"This is not a freeze of foreign portfolio investment, it simply regulates it," said Janko Tratnik, head of the foreign business department at the Bank of Slovenia.
Traders said share prices seemed to have bottomed out on Thursday and that selling pressure continued to subside.
"Share prices have already started to pick up again during today's session and are expected to stabilise at current levels tomorrow," one trader said.
"The first panic is over and demand has already started to grow in the belief that prices may have reached bottom," another broker said.
Overall 11 shares fell, seven rose and seven were untraded. Turnover rose to 343.3 million tolars from 74.3 million.
Issue A of drug company Lek was the most actively traded, falling 3.75 percent to 26,690 tolars on volume of 7,160 shares for total turnover of 181.3 million tolars.
Preferred shares of Dolenjska banka were the leading decliners, tumbling 14.76 percent to 12,360 on volume of 78 shares.
Pharmaceutical trader Salus was the biggest gainer, surging 7.86 percent to 15,100 on volume of 240 shares.
